GDS-15 Geriatric Depression Scale — FHIR Questionnaire Template

Yes/no questions screening older adults for depression, with an automatic total score and interpretation.

Open in Builder

Scoring

Each depressive answer scores 1 point (No on questions 1, 5, 7, 11 and 13; Yes on the rest). The total (0–15) suggests depression above 5.

Questions

  1. Are you basically satisfied with your life?
    • Yes
    • No
  2. Have you dropped many of your activities and interests?
    • Yes
    • No
  3. Do you feel that your life is empty?
    • Yes
    • No
  4. Do you often get bored?
    • Yes
    • No
  5. Are you in good spirits most of the time?
    • Yes
    • No
  6. Are you afraid that something bad is going to happen to you?
    • Yes
    • No
  7. Do you feel happy most of the time?
    • Yes
    • No
  8. Do you often feel helpless?
    • Yes
    • No
  9. Do you prefer to stay at home, rather than going out and doing new things?
    • Yes
    • No
  10. Do you feel you have more problems with memory than most?
    • Yes
    • No
  11. Do you think it is wonderful to be alive now?
    • Yes
    • No
  12. Do you feel pretty worthless the way you are now?
    • Yes
    • No
  13. Do you feel full of energy?
    • Yes
    • No
  14. Do you feel that your situation is hopeless?
    • Yes
    • No
  15. Do you think that most people are better off than you are?
    • Yes
    • No

Calculated results

  • GDS-15 total score (0–15)
  • Screening result

Source and license

Source: Sheikh & Yesavage 1986, Clin Gerontol 5:165 (GDS short form, from Yesavage et al. 1983, J Psychiatr Res 17:37). Codes: LOINC. (link)

License: The original scale is in the public domain; neither the GDS nor its electronic form is protected by copyright (per the scale author, J. A. Yesavage). (link)

Provided to save authoring effort, not as medical advice — confirm the scale and its cut-offs for your use case.

Use it

  1. Download the FHIR Questionnaire JSON, or
  2. open it in the Builder right away (or open the Builder, choose + Add → From template… and search for “GDS-15 Geriatric Depression Scale”). It arrives as one titled group with its calculations wired, and you can keep editing it.
